The control device is used to control delivery of fluids from a multi-fluid delivery system during a medical injection procedure. The fluid delivery system includes an injector used to deliver injection fluids to a patient. The control device is operatively associated with the injector for controlling discrete flow rates of injection fluids delivered to the patient. The control device includes first and second actuators associated with the manual control device, and an electronic substrate disposed within the manual control device and having a conductive pattern. The first actuator is operatively associated with the conductive pattern. The conductive pattern includes a plurality of predetermined digital values corresponding to discrete flow rates of injection fluids to be delivered by the injector. The second actuator is operatively associated with the electronic substrate and initiates output signals to the injector corresponding to desired mixture ratios of the injection fluids to be delivered by the injector.

The control device is functionally connected to the injector so that it can regulate separate, selectable flow rates of the fluids being delivered.

outputs.L3:
The control device is configured to regulate the delivery of fluids from a multi-fluid delivery system during a medical injection procedure. The multi-fluid delivery system includes an injector that delivers one or more injection fluids to a patient, such as contrast media, saline, or another medically appropriate fluid.

The control device is operatively connected to the injector and is used to control the flow of the injection fluids during the procedure. In particular, the control device enables selection and regulation of discrete flow rates for the injection fluids delivered by the injector. By controlling these flow rates, the device assists in managing the timing, quantity, and composition of the fluids administered to the patient.

The control device includes a first actuator and a second actuator. These actuators are arranged to allow a user, such as a clinician or technician, to input control commands for the injection procedure. The control device also includes an internal electronic substrate having a conductive pattern formed thereon. The conductive pattern is configured to generate or provide digital values corresponding to selected flow rates. These digital values are communicated to the injector or associated control electronics to regulate the delivery of the injection fluids at the desired discrete flow rates.

The second actuator is configured to initiate signals corresponding to desired mixture ratios of the injection fluids. In this way, the user may select or adjust the relative proportions of the fluids being delivered during the injection procedure. The control device therefore provides both flow-rate control and mixture-ratio control for the multi-fluid delivery system, enabling controlled and flexible administration of injection fluids to the patient.
outputs.L4:
A manual control device is provided for use with a multi-fluid medical injection system, such as an injector configured to deliver two or more medical fluids to a patient during a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. The device allows an operator to manually adjust and control the delivery of the fluids without directly operating the injector mechanisms themselves. In this way, the manual control device serves as an interface between the operator and the injector control system.

The control device includes a first actuator and a second actuator, each arranged to be manipulated by the operator. The first actuator may be used to select or control a desired total flow rate of fluid delivery from the injection system. The second actuator may be used to select or control the relative proportions of the fluids being delivered, such as the mixture ratio between a first fluid and a second fluid. For example, the first fluid may be a contrast agent and the second fluid may be saline, although other medical fluids may also be used.

The first and second actuators are operatively connected to an electronic substrate. The electronic substrate includes a conductive pattern configured to generate electrical signals corresponding to the positions or movements of the actuators. In particular, the conductive pattern associated with the first actuator provides a plurality of preset digital values. Each preset digital value corresponds to a discrete flow rate setting for the injector system. As the first actuator is moved between different positions, the control device outputs a digital signal identifying the selected flow rate. The injector control system then uses that signal to regulate the delivery rate of the fluid or fluids.

The second actuator is also linked to the electronic substrate and is configured to provide signals representing a desired mixture ratio of the fluids. By manipulating the second actuator, the operator can adjust the relative amount of each fluid delivered by the injector system. For instance, the operator may increase the proportion of one fluid while decreasing the proportion of another, while maintaining the selected overall flow rate. The signals from the second actuator are transmitted to the injector control system, which interprets the signals and controls the injector components accordingly.

Together, the first and second actuators enable independent or coordinated control of flow rate and fluid mixture. The conductive pattern on the electronic substrate provides reliable electrical outputs that can be interpreted by the injection system as discrete commands or settings. This arrangement permits controlled, repeatable, and adjustable delivery of multiple injection fluids to a patient. It also allows the operator to make changes during a procedure in a straightforward manner, improving the flexibility and responsiveness of the medical injection system.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it is also one of the most important. It is called a definite article, and its main purpose is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word helps make communication clearer. For example, “I saw a dog” introduces an unknown dog, while “I saw the dog” suggests that both speaker and listener know which dog is being discussed. In this way, “the” adds precision and context to everyday language.

The word is also extremely common. It appears in conversations, books, newspapers, songs, and speeches. Because it is so frequently used, many people do not notice it, but without it, English would sound incomplete or unclear.

Although “the” is short, it plays a major role in meaning. It connects ideas, identifies specific objects, and helps sentences flow naturally. This proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.output: A manual control device for a multi-fluid medical injector comprises first and second manually movable actuators coupled to an electronic substrate carrying a conductive pattern, wherein movement of the first actuator selectively engages portions of the conductive pattern to generate discrete flow-rate setting signals for controlling delivery rate of the injector, and movement of the second actuator selectively engages portions of the conductive pattern to generate mixture-ratio control signals for regulating relative proportions of multiple fluids delivered by the injector.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a control device used during a medical injection procedure to regulate delivery of multiple fluids from an injector, including actuators for selecting flow rates and mixture ratios.
counterfactuals.output: A control device for use during a medical injection procedure is provided for regulating delivery of a plurality of fluids from an injector to a patient. The control device includes a housing and one or more user-operable actuators configured to generate control inputs during the injection procedure. A first actuator is operable to select or vary a total flow rate of fluid delivered by the injector, and a second actuator is operable to select or vary a mixture ratio between at least two fluids, such as contrast medium and diluent. A controller communicates with the actuators and the injector and is configured to generate corresponding command signals for controlling operation of one or more drive mechanisms associated with respective fluid reservoirs. The controller may adjust individual fluid delivery rates to maintain the selected total flow rate while changing the selected mixture ratio, or to maintain the selected mixture ratio while changing the total flow rate. The control device enables real-time adjustment of fluid delivery parameters during the medical injection procedure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of a handheld controller for a multi-fluid delivery system, where one actuator selects discrete digital flow-rate values from a conductive pattern and another actuator sends mixture-ratio commands to an injector.
counterfactuals.output:
A handheld controller for a multi-fluid delivery system may include a compact housing configured to be gripped by an operator and coupled electrically to a remote control unit or directly to electrically actuated fluid-delivery components. The controller provides separate manual inputs for total flow-rate selection and mixture-ratio control.

The controller includes a first actuator, such as a rotary knob, thumbwheel, slide member, or indexed lever, mechanically coupled to an electrical contact element. The contact element moves relative to a conductive pattern disposed on a substrate, such as a printed circuit board. The conductive pattern defines a plurality of discrete contact regions corresponding to predetermined digital flow-rate values. As the first actuator is moved between indexed positions, the contact element selectively engages one or more regions of the conductive pattern, producing a digital selection signal representative of a selected flow rate. The conductive pattern may be arranged as concentric arcuate tracks, linear traces, or a coded contact matrix to provide binary, Gray-code, or position-specific outputs. Detents may be provided so that the first actuator remains aligned with each discrete flow-rate setting during operation.

A second actuator is provided independently of the first actuator to command a desired mixture ratio between two or more fluids supplied to an injector or mixing head. The second actuator may comprise a trigger, rocker, slider, rotary control, or proportional input device. Movement of the second actuator generates an electrical mixture-ratio command signal that is transmitted to an injector control circuit. The injector control circuit adjusts one or more metering valves, pumps, solenoids, or electronically controlled injector elements to vary the relative delivery of the fluids according to the commanded ratio. In one implementation, the second actuator provides a proportional analog signal; in another implementation, it provides incremental or digital ratio commands.

The handheld controller may further include signal-conditioning circuitry, pull-up or pull-down networks, debounce circuitry for the digital flow-rate contacts, and an output connector or cable for communication with the fluid delivery system. A processor or interface module may interpret the selected digital flow-rate value from the conductive pattern and combine it with the mixture-ratio command to generate control instructions for the injector. The total delivered flow may therefore be set in discrete steps by the first actuator, while the composition of the delivered mixture is varied by the second actuator.

The housing may include sealing features, strain relief, tactile indicators, position markings, and ergonomic surfaces suitable for field or clinical use. The controller may also include indicators, such as LEDs or a display, to show the selected flow-rate value, mixture-ratio setting, system status, or fault conditions. This arrangement allows an operator to quickly select repeatable discrete flow rates while independently adjusting or commanding the ratio of multiple fluids delivered through the injector.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a broad patent disclosure paragraph for a medical fluid injection control device operatively connected to an injector, emphasizing discrete flow rate control through a conductive pattern and mixture ratio signal initiation through a second actuator.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, a medical fluid injection control device is provided for operative connection to a medical fluid injector configured to deliver one or more medical fluids to a patient. The control device may include a housing, a user-actuatable flow control member, and an electrical interface configured to communicate control signals to the injector. The flow control member may be movable among a plurality of discrete positions, each position corresponding to a respective predetermined flow rate or flow rate command. A conductive pattern, such as a plurality of conductive traces, pads, contacts, resistive elements, or coded electrical pathways, may be disposed on or associated with a substrate within the control device such that movement of the flow control member selectively establishes one or more electrical connections with the conductive pattern to generate a discrete flow rate control signal for the injector. The device may further include a second actuator, separate from or integrated with the flow control member, configured to initiate a mixture ratio signal associated with a selected or desired ratio of a plurality of medical fluids to be delivered by the injector. Actuation of the second actuator may cause the electrical interface to transmit the mixture ratio signal to the injector, either independently of or in combination with the discrete flow rate control signal, thereby enabling the injector to control delivery of the medical fluids according to both a selected discrete flow rate and a selected mixture ratio. The conductive pattern and the second actuator may be configured in various mechanical, electrical, analog, digital, wired, or wireless implementations without departing from the scope of the disclosure.
